intro: A wet room is one of the most practical and stylish bathroom upgrades you can make to a Bromley home, but it's also one of the more technically demanding — and the cost reflects that. That range might sound wide, but it covers a lot of ground: a straightforward conversion in a modern flat looks very different from a full structural waterproofing job in a Victorian terrace. Done well, a wet room adds genuine value to a property and can transform daily life for people with mobility needs or simply those who want a cleaner, more minimal space.
localContext: Bromley's housing stock is genuinely varied, and that variety matters when you're planning a wet room. The borough has a substantial number of Victorian and Edwardian terraces — particularly in areas like Shortlands, Beckenham, and parts of Bromley town itself — where original timber floor joists need careful assessment before any wet room work begins. Older floors may require reinforcement or replacement to support the additional weight of a tanked, tiled surface. Post-war semis and bungalows, common across much of the borough, often have more straightforward concrete ground floors but can present challenges with older pipework and limited ceiling height. Newer flats and modern builds in the Bromley town centre regeneration areas tend to be easier to work with structurally, though building regulations and lease agreements may add their own complications. Bromley also sits in a moderately hard water area, which means limescale build-up on screen-free wet room floors and walls is a real consideration — your installer should advise on appropriate sealants and grout types to make ongoing maintenance manageable.
serviceDetail: A professional wet room installation in Bromley follows a clear sequence, and understanding it helps you know what you're actually paying for. The process begins with a thorough survey of the existing bathroom — checking floor structure, drainage routes, existing plumbing, and the condition of walls. If the floor needs reinforcing or levelling, that groundwork happens first. The next stage is tanking: the application of a waterproof membrane to the floor and walls, which is the most critical part of the job. This is not a step to cut corners on, as poor tanking is the primary cause of wet room failures. Once tanking is complete and cured, a former is installed to create the correct fall towards the drain — typically a linear drain running along one wall or a central point drain. Tiling or surface finishing then takes place, followed by the installation of fixtures: the shower valve, head, screen if required, and any heated towel rail or underfloor heating. Final first and second fix plumbing connects everything to the existing supply and waste system. The whole process typically takes five to ten working days depending on complexity, and you should expect the bathroom to be out of use throughout. A reputable installer will also provide a guarantee on the waterproofing work — ask specifically about this before agreeing to any quote in Bromley.
pricing: In Bromley, a basic wet room conversion — replacing a standard shower enclosure in a structurally sound modern bathroom with minimal reconfiguration — typically starts around £6,000 to £7,500. A mid-range project with new floor structure work, quality tiling, underfloor heating, and a thermostatic shower system sits more comfortably in the £8,000 to £10,000 bracket. At the top end, particularly in larger Victorian properties where significant structural and waterproofing work is needed, or where high-specification finishes are chosen, costs can reach £12,000 or beyond. Labour, waterproofing materials, drainage, and tiling are the biggest cost drivers — don't let anyone persuade you to save money by underspecifying the waterproofing membrane.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Bromley well genuinely makes a difference with a project like this. A local installer will have worked in the borough's range of property types — they'll know the quirks of older Victorian floors in Shortlands, the drainage constraints you sometimes find in post-war properties in Petts Wood, and what building control in Bromley typically expects for this kind of work. They're also easier to hold accountable if something needs attention after the job is complete. Word-of-mouth reputation matters in a community like Bromley, and a good local wet room specialist has a strong reason to get every job right.

faqs.q: Is my Victorian Bromley terrace suitable for a wet room?
faqs.a: Many Victorian terraces in Bromley can accommodate a wet room, but the timber floor structure usually needs assessment first. A structural survey may be needed, and in some cases the floor will require reinforcement or a new concrete screed. It's very doable, but budget for this groundwork — it's not optional, and a good installer will flag it upfront.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Bromley?
faqs.a: Most wet room projects in Bromley take between five and ten working days from strip-out to completion. More complex jobs — particularly in older properties needing structural work or significant replumbing — can take closer to two weeks. You'll be without a functioning bathroom during this time, so it's worth planning access to an alternative facility or timing the work carefully.

faqs.q: Will Bromley's hard water cause problems with my wet room?
faqs.a: Bromley is in a moderately hard water area, so limescale is a genuine consideration. In a wet room without a full enclosure, water dries on tiles and grout more visibly than in a traditional shower. Choosing a large-format tile with minimal grout lines, using a good penetrating sealant, and installing a water softener or shower head filter all help reduce maintenance. Your installer should discuss this during the design phase.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a wet room in Bromley?
faqs.a: In most cases, no planning permission is required for a wet room conversion in Bromley — it falls under permitted development. However, if you live in a listed building or a conservation area (there are several in the borough), you may need to check with Bromley Council first. Building regulations will apply regardless, particularly around waterproofing, drainage, and ventilation, and a competent installer will handle this as part of the job.
